posts.title: 39 Gold Metallic Nail Ideas in 2026
posts.excerpt: Gold metallic nails, all 39 of them: true mirror gold, champagne chrome, rose gold shine, gold French tips and foil-gold glam, on almond, coffin, square, oval and short shapes and every skin tone, with photos and exactly what to ask your nail tech for.
intro: Gold is the warm metal, and in chrome form it reads like jewelry you never take off. These **39 gold metallic nail ideas** collect the whole range: true mirror gold, soft champagne chrome, rose gold shine, gold French tips and foil-gold party sets, on almond, coffin, stiletto, square, oval and short shapes. Every set is on real hands and real skin tones, dark and brown skin included throughout, and every photo below is drawn from the 123 gold metallic designs video on the NailDex channel.

Pick your gold before you book. Yellow mirror gold is the boldest and reads richest on warm skin; champagne gold is the soft everyday version; rose gold chrome sits in between and flatters everyone. Gold French tips keep the metal only at the edge for the office-safe take. Shapes follow the metal: almond and oval show the mirror unbroken, coffin carries the full glam brief. The full collection lives in the Gold Metallic topic hub, and the rest of the season is in the inspo journal.

A booking note from the tech chair: metallic chrome lives or dies on the base. Ask for a smooth, fully cured gel base, chrome powder rubbed in and sealed with a hard gel top coat, free edge sealed at every layer, so the gold does not rub off at the tips. Save this page, pick your set, and show your nail tech the photo: each design below includes the exact words to ask for.

faq.q: What shades of gold chrome are there?
faq.a: Yellow mirror gold is the richest, champagne gold the softest, and rose gold chrome the in-between flatterer: design 1 (Gold Mirror Stiletto on Dark Skin) shows the full mirror, while design 11 (Gold Glitter Coffin Duo) shows the softer everyday take.

faq.q: Do gold metallic nails work on short nails?
faq.a: Yes. Gold chrome wraps short shapes beautifully and reads like jewelry at any length. Design 4 (Gold Mirror Almond Clasped) and design 21 (Gold Swirl Almond Duo on Dark Skin Bright) prove the shine keeps its impact short.

faq.q: What gold nails look best on dark skin?
faq.a: Warm mirror gold is a standout on dark and brown skin: the metal glows against deeper skin and never reads dull. See design 2 (Champagne Gold Almond in Knit), design 16 (Gold Mirror Square Close-Up) and design 31 (Gold French Short Duo with Rings).

faq.q: How do I keep gold chrome from rubbing off at the tips?
faq.a: Sealing is everything. Ask for chrome sealed under a hard gel top coat with the free edge sealed at every layer, like design 26 (Gold Glitter Almond Duo Palms), and re-oil cuticles daily.

faq.q: Can gold metallic nails be worn every day?
faq.a: Yes, in the champagne and French versions. A soft gold like design 16 (Gold Mirror Square Close-Up) reads polished at work; save the full mirror for the statement days.

intro: Emerald is the jewel of the green family: deeper than sage, richer than forest, and it flatters every skin tone it touches. These **36 emerald green nail ideas** collect the whole range: true emerald gloss, deep green chrome, velvet and cat eye finishes, emerald-and-gold glam, marble greens and green French tips, on almond, coffin, stiletto, square, oval and short shapes. Every set is on real hands and real skin tones, dark and brown skin included throughout, and every photo below is drawn from the 123 emerald green designs video on the NailDex channel.

Pick your emerald before you book. The glossy jewel version is the everyday signature: polished, rich, and it hides regrowth for weeks. Velvet and cat eye greens are the light-catching party picks, chrome green is the metal statement, and emerald with gold accents is the holiday-season glam. Shapes follow the color: almond and oval keep it elegant, coffin and stiletto carry the drama, short square emerald is the practical rich pick. The full collection lives in the Emerald Green topic hub, and the rest of the season is in the inspo journal.

A booking note from the tech chair: deep green pigment needs thin, fully cured layers or it wrinkles and fades at the edges. Ask for gel built in thin coats, a hard gel top coat, and the free edge sealed at every layer so the jewel tone stays deep. Save this page, pick your set, and show your nail tech the photo: each design below includes the exact words to ask for.

faq.q: What shades count as emerald green nails?
faq.a: True emerald is the deep jewel green; the family runs from bright jewel gloss to near-black deep green. Design 1 (Emerald Almond) shows the classic jewel, while design 11 (Emerald Almond with Gold Glitter Accent) shows the deeper evening version.

faq.q: Do emerald green nails work on short nails?
faq.a: Yes. Deep green concentrates beautifully at short length and short square emerald is a signature rich look. Design 4 (Emerald Cat Eye Oval Duo) and design 21 (Emerald Chrome Almond with Gold Rings) prove the color keeps its depth short.

faq.q: What emerald green nails look best on dark skin?
faq.a: Emerald is one of the great colors on dark and brown skin: the jewel tone reads rich and luminous, never muddy, especially with gold accents. See design 2 (Dark Emerald Oval with Orchid), design 16 (Emerald Short Square Duo) and design 31 (Emerald Coffin with Glitter Accent in Towel).

faq.q: How do I keep dark green nails from fading or wrinkling?
faq.a: Thin layers, fully cured, sealed under a hard gel top coat with the free edge sealed at every layer, like design 26 (Emerald Gold Foil Square Close-Up); deep pigments punish thick coats.

faq.q: Are emerald nails only for winter?
faq.a: They peak in the holiday season but wear all year: a clean emerald like design 16 (Emerald Short Square Duo) is an everyday signature, and the velvet versions carry the party months.

posts.title: 39 Snowflake Nail Ideas in 2026
posts.excerpt: Snowflake nails, all 39 of them: hand-painted flakes on icy blue, white and deep winter bases, silver glitter frost, pearl and chrome snow finishes and snowflake French tips, on almond, coffin, square, oval and short shapes and every skin tone, with photos and exactly what to ask your nail tech for.
intro: Snowflakes are the signature art of the winter set: fine white linework, icy bases and frost that catches the light. These **39 snowflake nail ideas** collect the whole range: classic white flakes on icy blue and deep winter bases, silver glitter frost, pearl and chrome snow finishes, and snowflake French tips, on almond, coffin, stiletto, square, oval and short shapes. Every set is on real hands and real skin tones, dark and brown skin included throughout, and every photo below is drawn from the 123 snowflake designs video on the NailDex channel.

Pick your flake before you book. The hand-painted version on a deep base is the statement: high contrast, unmistakably winter. Glitter frost is the party pick, pearl and milky white are the soft everyday versions, and a snowflake accent nail over a clean French is the minimal route. Shapes follow the art: almond and coffin give the flakes canvas, short square keeps it practical. The full collection lives in the Snowflake topic hub, and the rest of the season is in the inspo journal.

A booking note from the tech chair: snowflake linework is only as good as its cure. Ask for thin white gel lines, flash-cured flake by flake so nothing bleeds, and everything sealed under a hard top coat. Save this page, pick your set, and show your nail tech the photo: each design below includes the exact words to ask for.

faq.q: What base colors work best under snowflake nails?
faq.a: Any base with contrast: icy blue, navy, burgundy and deep green make white flakes pop, while milky white and pearl give the soft tone-on-tone look. Design 1 (Snowflake Ombre Coffin Duo) shows the classic contrast version, while design 11 (Blue French Snowflake Duo) shows the softer route.

faq.q: Do snowflake nails work on short nails?
faq.a: Yes. One small flake per nail reads perfectly at short length, and short square snowflakes are a signature winter look. Design 4 (Grey Knit Snowflake Oval) and design 21 (French Snowflake Square with Rings) prove the art keeps its detail short.

faq.q: What snowflake nails look best on dark skin?
faq.a: Snowflakes are brilliant on dark and brown skin: white linework and icy bases read bright and crisp, never washed out, especially over deep blue or burgundy. See design 2 (Royal Blue Snowflake Oval Duo), design 16 (Glitter Tip Snowflake Short) and design 31 (Pearl Chrome Snowflakes in Knit).

faq.q: How do I keep fine snowflake linework from chipping?
faq.a: Thin gel lines, flash-cured as they are painted, then sealed under a hard top coat, like design 26 (Milky Snowflake Short); thick uncured lines are what lift and blur.

faq.q: Are snowflake nails only for Christmas week?
faq.a: They peak in December but wear all winter: a clean snowflake like design 16 (Glitter Tip Snowflake Short) is a January signature too, long after the tree comes down.

posts.title: 38 Velvet Red Nail Ideas in 2026
posts.excerpt: Velvet red nails, all 38 of them: magnetic cat-eye velvet, deep wine and burgundy velvets, black-red ombres, matte flock velvet, red velvet French tips and glitter velvets, on almond, coffin, square, oval and short shapes and every skin tone, with photos and exactly what to ask your nail tech for.
intro: Velvet is the finish that made red magnetic: a cat-eye stripe that rolls across the nail like light on fabric. These **38 velvet red nail ideas** collect the whole range: true velvet cat eye, deep wine and burgundy velvets, black-red ombres, true matte flock velvet, red velvet French tips and glitter velvets, on almond, coffin, stiletto, square, oval and short shapes. Every set is on real hands and real skin tones, dark and brown skin included throughout, and every photo below is drawn from the 123 velvet red designs video on the NailDex channel.

Pick your velvet before you book. The centered-stripe gloss version is the everyday signature: rich, dimensional, and it hides regrowth for weeks. Black-red ombre velvet is the dramatic evening pick, matte flock is the true fabric look, and a red velvet French tip is the minimal route. Shapes follow the finish: almond and coffin give the stripe room to roll, short square velvet is the practical rich pick. The full collection lives in the Velvet Red topic hub, and the rest of the season is in the inspo journal.

A booking note from the tech chair: velvet is a magnet technique, not a polish. Ask for magnetic gel, the magnet held close for a few seconds on every nail before curing, and a second magnet pass over the top coat if you want the stripe at full strength. Save this page, pick your set, and show your nail tech the photo: each design below includes the exact words to ask for.

faq.q: What exactly are velvet nails?
faq.a: Velvet nails use magnetic gel polish: a magnet pulls the particles into a soft band of light that shifts as the nail moves, like velvet fabric. Design 1 (Velvet Red Stiletto Duo) shows the classic centered stripe, while design 11 (Red Chrome Coffin Close-Up) shows the darker ombre version.

faq.q: Do velvet red nails work on short nails?
faq.a: Yes. The stripe concentrates beautifully at short length and short square velvet red is a signature rich look. Design 4 (Red Black Ombre Coffin) and design 21 (Velvet Red Almond Duo on Fur) prove the effect keeps its depth short.

faq.q: What velvet red nails look best on dark skin?
faq.a: Velvet red is luminous on dark and brown skin: the magnetic band reads like lit fabric and deep wine shades never go muddy. See design 2 (Velvet Red Cat Eye Almond), design 16 (Velvet Foil Almond in Knit) and design 31 (Red Black Ombre Stiletto Duo).

faq.q: How do I keep the velvet stripe strong?
faq.a: The magnet pass is everything: held close a few seconds per nail before curing, and repeated over the top coat, like design 26 (Red Glitter Velvet Cherry Accent); a rushed magnet pass is what makes velvet look flat.

faq.q: Are velvet red nails only for the holidays?
faq.a: They peak in party season but wear all year: a clean velvet red like design 16 (Velvet Foil Almond in Knit) is an everyday signature, and the black-red versions carry the evening months.

posts.title: 36 Winter Almond Nail Ideas in 2026
posts.excerpt: Winter almond nails, all 36 of them: milky whites and snow-day nudes, cocoa and burgundy almonds, navy and forest winter shades, plaid and sweater textures, chrome and glitter finishes and winter French tips, on real hands and every skin tone, with photos and exactly what to ask your nail tech for.
intro: Almond is the shape winter was made for: elegant like a stiletto, practical like an oval, and long enough to carry every cold-weather shade. These **36 winter almond nail ideas** collect the whole season: milky whites and snow-day nudes, cocoa and burgundy almonds, navy and forest winter shades, plaid and sweater textures, chrome and glitter finishes and winter French tips. Every set is on real hands and real skin tones, dark and brown skin included throughout, and every photo below is drawn from the 123 winter almond designs video on the NailDex channel.

Pick your winter lane before you book. Milky white and nude almonds are the everyday signatures: soft, brightening, and they hide regrowth for weeks. Cocoa, burgundy and navy are the rich winter picks, plaid and sweater textures are the cozy statement, and chrome is the party finish. Length follows lifestyle: medium almond is the sweet spot that survives gloves and typing. The full collection lives in the Winter Almond topic hub, and the rest of the season is in the inspo journal.

A booking note from the tech chair: winter is hard on nails, so the shape matters. Almond distributes stress better than square corners, which is why these sets survive the dry season; ask for gel or gel extensions, cuticle oil daily, and bring the photo of your pick: each design below includes the exact words to ask for.

faq.q: Why is almond the best winter shape?
faq.a: Almond has no sharp corners to catch on gloves, coats and knits, and the tapered sides distribute stress, so sets survive the dry season better. Design 1 (Burgundy Snowflake Almond on Fur) shows the classic medium almond most of this list is built on.

faq.q: What winter colors suit almond nails best?
faq.a: Milky whites and nudes for everyday, cocoa and burgundy for richness, navy and forest for drama. See design 4 (Chocolate Almond with Gold Ring) for the soft end and design 21 (Emerald Silver Almond Duo) for the deep shades.

faq.q: Do winter almond nails work on dark skin?
faq.a: Beautifully: winter shades glow on dark and brown skin and milky tones brighten against it. See design 2 (Emerald Leaf Art Almond), design 16 (Plaid Mix Short Almond Duo) and design 31 (Blue French Almond Duo in Snow).

faq.q: What length should winter almonds be?
faq.a: Medium is the sweet spot: long enough for the elegant taper, short enough for gloves and typing, like design 26 (Nude French Snowflake Almond); go longer only for party weeks.

faq.q: How do I stop winter nails breaking?
faq.a: The almond shape itself helps; add gel or gel extensions for strength, cuticle oil daily against dry air, and a shape like design 11 (White Line Art Almond on Dark Skin) with no square corners to snag.

posts.title: 37 Icy Blue Nail Ideas in 2026
posts.excerpt: Icy blue nails, all 37 of them: pale ice and baby blue, frosty chrome and glazed finishes, icy French tips, glitter frost, snow-day marble and cat eye ice, on almond, coffin, square, oval and short shapes and every skin tone, with photos and exactly what to ask your nail tech for.
intro: Icy blue is the frozen end of the winter palette: pale, glassy and cold in the best way. These **37 icy blue nail ideas** collect the whole range: pale ice and baby blue, frosty chrome and glazed finishes, icy French tips, glitter frost, snow-day marble and cat eye ice, with deep frozen navy for contrast. Every set is on real hands and real skin tones, dark and brown skin included throughout, and every photo below is drawn from the 123 icy blue designs video on the NailDex channel.

Pick your ice level before you book. Pale milky blue is the everyday signature: clean, brightening, and it hides regrowth for weeks. Frosty chrome and glazed ice are the statement finishes, an icy French tip is the minimal route, and glitter frost is the party pick. Shapes follow the finish: almond and oval keep it soft, square makes it crisp. The full collection lives in the Icy Blue topic hub, and the rest of the season is in the inspo journal.

A booking note from the tech chair: icy blue is unforgiving about shade. Too warm and it reads baby shower, too grey and it goes dull; the sweet spot is a cool, slightly translucent blue, ideally over a milky base. Save this page, pick your set, and show your nail tech the photo: each design below includes the exact words to ask for.

faq.q: What counts as icy blue?
faq.a: A cool, pale blue with a frozen, glassy feel: think ice, frost and glacier water rather than sky. Design 1 (Icy Blue Coffin Crystal Accent) is the reference shade, while design 11 (Baby Blue Stiletto Snowflakes) shows the chrome version.

faq.q: Do icy blue nails work on dark skin?
faq.a: Yes, and they pop: the pale cool blue contrasts beautifully with dark and brown skin and the chrome versions glow. See design 2 (Grey Blue Snowflake Almond), design 16 (Blue Ombre Chrome Almond) and design 31 (Silver Chrome Almond at Pinecones).

faq.q: Icy blue or baby blue: what is the difference?
faq.a: Baby blue is warmer and creamier; icy blue is cooler, paler and usually translucent or glazed. Design 4 (Baby Blue Ombre Coffin on Dark Skin) sits on the icy side, while the softest sets here lean baby.

faq.q: What finish makes blue look frozen?
faq.a: Chrome rubs, glazed (milky glass) top coats and fine glitter frost. Design 21 (Blue Snowflake Chrome Duo) shows the glazed route; ask for the same finish at any length.

faq.q: Are icy blue nails only for winter?
faq.a: They peak in winter but the pale chrome versions wear as a cool neutral all year; a clean icy set like design 26 (Periwinkle Glitter Snowflake Duo) is seasonless.

posts.excerpt: Pearl white nails, all 38 of them: glazed pearl chrome and iridescent shine, milky pearl whites, bridal-clean French tips and pearl accent nails, on almond, coffin, square, oval and short shapes and every skin tone, with photos and exactly what to ask your nail tech for.
intro: Pearl white is the luminous end of the white palette: glazed, glowing and clean in the best way. These **38 pearl white nail ideas** collect the whole range: glazed pearl chrome and iridescent shine, milky pearl whites, bridal-clean French tips and pearl accent nails, with soft shimmer finishes throughout. Every set is on real hands and real skin tones, dark and brown skin included throughout, and every photo below is drawn from the 123 pearl white designs video on the NailDex channel.

Pick your glow level before you book. Milky pearl is the everyday signature: clean, brightening, and it hides regrowth for weeks. Glazed chrome pearl is the statement finish, a pearl French tip is the minimal route, and a single pearl accent nail is the subtle pick. Shapes follow the finish: almond and oval keep it soft, square makes it crisp. The full collection lives in the Pearl White topic hub, and the rest of the season is in the inspo journal.

A booking note from the tech chair: pearl white is unforgiving about base color. Too stark and it reads chalky, too sheer and it disappears; the sweet spot is a milky white under a pearl chrome rub. Save this page, pick your set, and show your nail tech the photo: each design below includes the exact words to ask for.

faq.q: What counts as pearl white?
faq.a: A luminous white with a pearlescent glow: think glazed, iridescent and softly shiny rather than flat white. Design 1 (Full Pearl Coffin on Dark Skin) is the reference finish, while design 11 (Pearl Chrome Short Duo in Knit) shows the chrome version.

faq.q: Do pearl white nails work on dark skin?
faq.a: Yes, beautifully: the luminous white contrasts and glows on dark and brown skin. See design 2 (Pearl Cluster Square on Cotton), design 16 (Pearl Cluster Coffin in Palm on Dark Skin) and design 31 (Pearl Chrome Short Duo on Silk).

faq.q: Pearl white or milky white: what is the difference?
faq.a: Milky white is a soft translucent white with no shimmer; pearl white adds the pearlescent chrome glow on top. Design 4 (Glossy Pearl Almond Duo) sits on the pearl side, while the softest sets here lean milky.

faq.q: What finish makes white look luminous?
faq.a: Pearl chrome rubs, glazed top coats and fine iridescent shimmer. Design 21 (Opal Pearl Oval in Palm) shows the glazed route; ask for the same finish at any length.

faq.q: Are pearl white nails only for weddings?
faq.a: They peak at weddings but the clean pearl versions wear as a polished neutral all year; a set like design 26 (Blue Pearl Oval Duo with Ring) is seasonless.

faq.a: A mirror-metallic finish in a warm pink-gold tone, usually chrome powder rubbed over a blush or nude gel base. Design 1 (Mirror Rose Gold Stiletto Duo on Dark Skin) is the reference shine, while design 11 (Blush Jelly Almond with Chrome Edge) shows the softer metallic version.

faq.q: Do rose gold chrome nails work on dark skin?
faq.a: Yes, they glow: the warm metal flatters dark and brown skin especially. See design 2 (Mirror Rose Gold Oval Macro), design 16 (Gold Glitter Chrome Coffin Duo) and design 31 (Rose Chrome Stiletto Duo Duo).

faq.q: Rose gold chrome or pink chrome: what is the difference?
faq.a: Pink chrome is cooler and more candy-toned; rose gold is warmer, with the gold pulling it toward jewelry metal. Design 4 (Black Art Almond with Rose Glitter) sits on the rose gold side.

faq.q: How long does chrome last?
faq.a: With a structured gel base and a no-wipe top coat, chrome wears like regular gel: two to three weeks. Design 21 (Silver Tip Ombre Stiletto Duo) shows the full-mirror version worth protecting.

faq.q: Can rose gold chrome be subtle?
faq.a: Yes: a French tip or a single chrome accent nail keeps it office-friendly. Design 26 (Blush Chrome Short Duo) is the restrained route.

posts.title: 36 Short Winter Nail Ideas in 2026
posts.excerpt: Short winter nails, all 36 of them: snowflake art and frosty whites, short burgundy and deep red, cozy glitter, short French tips and winter neutrals at practical lengths, on square, oval, almond and round shapes and every skin tone, with photos and exactly what to ask your nail tech for.
intro: Short winter is the practical end of the cold-season palette: every winter design, at a length you can type, cook and live in. These **36 short winter nail ideas** collect the whole range: snowflake art and frosty whites, short burgundy and deep red, cozy glitter and short French tips, navy and winter neutrals. Every set is on real hands and real skin tones, dark and brown skin included throughout, and every photo below is drawn from the 180 short winter designs video on the NailDex channel.

Pick your winter mood before you book. Frosty white and snowflake art are the December signature, burgundy is the everyday classic, glitter is the party pick, and a short French tip is the minimal route. Shapes follow the hand: oval and almond soften short nails, square makes them crisp. The full collection lives in the Short Winter topic hub, and the rest of the season is in the inspo journal.

A booking note from the tech chair: short nails are a design constraint, not a compromise. Art has to be scaled, fine lines have to be finer, and dark colors need a clean edge to look expensive. Save this page, pick your set, and show your nail tech the photo: each design below includes the exact words to ask for.

faq.q: What counts as a short winter nail?
faq.a: A practical, near-fingertip length in a cold-season palette or design: frosty whites, snowflakes, burgundy, navy, cozy glitter. Design 1 (Nude Short with Snowflake Accent in Cream Knit) is the reference set, while design 11 (Christmas Mix Short Duo) shows the art-led version.

faq.q: Do short winter nails work on dark skin?
faq.a: Yes: deep winter colors and bright frosty whites both pop on dark and brown skin. See design 2 (Christmas Art Short Duo), design 16 (Blush Short Duo with Snowflake Accent in Purple Knit) and design 31 (Olive Short Duo with Tree Accent at Garland).

faq.q: Can you do nail art on short nails?
faq.a: Absolutely, it just has to be scaled: finer snowflakes, tip-concentrated designs, single-accent nails. Design 4 (Forest Green Short with Snowflake Accent) shows the scaled route done right.

faq.q: What shape is best for short winter nails?
faq.a: Oval and almond soften and lengthen the look of short nails; square is crisper and more modern. Design 21 (Snowflake Glitter Tip Short Duo in Knit) shows the soft route.

faq.q: How do short sets hold up in winter?
faq.a: Better than long ones: less leverage, fewer breaks, and gloves go on without a fight. A gel set like design 26 (Black Snowflake Short Duo Duo) easily lasts two to three weeks.

posts.title: 39 Plum Nail Ideas in 2026
posts.excerpt: Plum nails, all 39 of them: rich plum and dark eggplant, plum chrome and cat eye depth, plum glitter and marble, matte plum and French tips, on almond, coffin, square, oval and short shapes and every skin tone, with photos and exactly what to ask your nail tech for.
intro: Plum is the deep end of the purple palette: rich, wine-dark and dramatic in the best way. These **39 plum nail ideas** collect the whole range: rich plum and dark eggplant, plum chrome and cat eye depth, plum glitter and marble, matte plum and plum French tips. Every set is on real hands and real skin tones, dark and brown skin included throughout, and every photo below is drawn from the 198 plum designs video on the NailDex channel.

Pick your depth before you book. Glossy rich plum is the everyday signature: saturated, polished, seasonless-dark. Cat eye and chrome are the statement finishes, matte plum is the moody route, and a plum French tip is the minimal pick. Shapes follow the color: almond and coffin keep it elegant, square makes it sharp. The full collection lives in the Plum topic hub, and the rest of the season is in the inspo journal.

A booking note from the tech chair: plum is unforgiving about coats. Too thin and it goes patchy, too thick and it floods; the sweet spot is two thin, fully cured coats over a smooth base. Save this page, pick your set, and show your nail tech the photo: each design below includes the exact words to ask for.

faq.q: What counts as plum?
faq.a: A deep, wine-rich purple: darker and warmer than lavender or violet, lighter than near-black eggplant at its deepest. Design 1 (Deep Plum Matte with Chrome Gem Accents) is the reference shade, while design 11 (Burgundy Stiletto Duo on Fur) shows the chrome version.

faq.q: Do plum nails work on dark skin?
faq.a: Yes, they are made for each other: the rich purple glows on dark and brown skin. See design 2 (Plum Glitter Stiletto Duo), design 16 (Glossy Plum Almond Duo) and design 31 (Plum Cat Eye Almond Duo Duo).

faq.q: Plum or burgundy: what is the difference?
faq.a: Burgundy leans red-wine; plum leans purple-wine. Design 4 (Matte Violet Almond Duo Outdoors) sits firmly on the plum side, while the warmest sets here borrow a little burgundy light.

faq.q: What finish suits plum best?
faq.a: High gloss for richness, cat eye for dimension, matte for mood. Design 21 (Violet Coffin Duo with Gold Art) shows the dimensional route; ask for the same finish at any length.

faq.q: Are plum nails only for fall and winter?
faq.a: They peak in the cold months but a clean glossy plum wears as a rich neutral-dark all year; a set like design 26 (Plum Almond Duo in Cream Knit) is seasonless.

posts.title: 40 New Year's Eve Nail Ideas in 2026
posts.excerpt: New Year's Eve nails, all 40 of them: champagne gold and silver glitter, black-and-gold drama, midnight blue sparkle, confetti art and chrome party shine, on almond, coffin, square, oval and short shapes and every skin tone, with photos and exactly what to ask your nail tech for.
intro: New Year's Eve is the one night glitter is a dress code. These **40 New Year's Eve nail ideas** collect the whole countdown wardrobe: champagne gold and silver sparkle, black-and-gold drama, midnight blue glitter, confetti art and chrome party shine, on almond, coffin, stiletto, square, oval and short shapes. Every set is on real hands and real skin tones, dark and brown skin included throughout, and every photo below is drawn from the 123 New Year's Eve designs video on the NailDex channel.

Pick your midnight mood before you book. The metal sets (gold, silver and rose chrome with glitter) catch party light from across the room; the dark sets (black and gold, midnight blue, burgundy glitter) are the dramatic, photograph-all-night picks. Shapes follow the party too: stiletto and coffin carry the full glam brief, almond is the elegant middle, and short sparkle is the practical pick if you are working the night. The full collection lives in the New Year's Eve topic hub, and the rest of the season is in the inspo journal.

A booking note from the tech chair: NYE week is the busiest of the year, so book this set early and ask for glitter sealed under a hard gel top coat so the sparkle survives the night. Save this page, pick your set, and show your nail tech the photo: each design below includes the exact words to ask for.

faq.q: What nail colors are in for New Year's Eve 2026?
faq.a: Gold, silver and champagne glitter lead, with black-and-gold and midnight blue as the dramatic picks: design 1 (Black Gold Coffin on Dark Skin) shows the sparkle end, while design 11 (Silver Glitter Fur Cuff) shows the dark glam version wearing everywhere this season.

faq.q: Do NYE nails work on short nails?
faq.a: Yes. Glitter concentrates beautifully at short length, and a short sparkle set is the practical party pick. Design 4 (Confetti Glitter Short Almond) and design 21 (Silver Metallic Almond Palms) prove the range keeps its shine short.

faq.q: What New Year's Eve nails look best on dark skin?
faq.a: Gold glitter and silver chrome are the standouts on dark and brown skin: the metal glow reads rich and the sparkle never washes out. See design 2 (Pink Glitter Almond), design 16 (Silver Glitter Short Oval) and design 31 (Neon Party Art on Dark Skin).

faq.q: How do I keep glitter nails from snagging on party clothes?
faq.a: Sealing is everything. Ask for glitter fully encapsulated under a hard gel top coat with sealed free edges, like design 26 (Black Gold Art Short Square), and the surface stays glass-smooth all night.

faq.q: When should I book my New Year's Eve set?
faq.a: Early. Countdown week books out first, so lock the appointment as soon as you pick your design; a full-glam set like design 16 (Silver Glitter Short Oval) needs the long slot.
